problem: A particle starts moving from the point with position vector $(-i+2j)\,\text{km},$ with an acceleration of $(i-j)\,{\text{km/h}}^{2}$ and an initial velocity of $3j\,\text{km/h}.$ Find the distance from the particle to the origin after $4$ hours.
worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant acceleration $a,$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut+\frac{1}{2}a{t}^{2},
$$

 

where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle and $u$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=-i+2j,\,u=3j,\,a=i-j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t=4\,\text{h}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(-i+2j)+(3j)(4)+\frac{1}{2}(i-j)(4)^{2} \\  & =(-i+2j)+(12j)+8(i-j) \\  & =(-i+14j)+(8i-8j) \\  & =(7i+6j)\,\text{km}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance from the particle to the origin at this time is

$$
\begin{aligned}|r| & =|7i+6j| \\  & =\sqrt{{7}^{2}+{6}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{49+36} \\  & =\sqrt{85}\,\text{km}.\end{aligned}
$$
